![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14058551/assets/3a4526a6979a86aa924bddca54b05778e91bb67a1dcb6159c5436cc975b22668.png)

A cyclist records the total distance traveled after $x$ minutes. The total distance traveled after $x$ minutes, in miles, is given by the function $D(x).$ The graph of $D(x)$ is shown above.  

Approximate the rate of change when $x=45$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=15.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=30$ and $x=45.$*

The estimated rate of change when $x=45$ is
{{field-1}} miles per minute.
worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{D}^{′}(x)≈\frac{D(x)-D(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=45.$  Applying the above formula with $x=45$ and $h=15$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}^{′}(45) & ≈\frac{D(45)-D(45-15)}{15} \\  & =\frac{D(45)-D(30)}{15} \\  & =\frac{11-6}{15} \\  & =\frac{5}{15} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $x=45$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ miles per minute.
